text: Before creating or updating a shopping cart entry for a selected product, the system shall check product availability and confirm that the product can be added.
After successful login, the system shall redirect the authenticated customer to their own personalized dashboard.
When the User Interface Specification Compliance Checking Function is performed, the system shall generate a compliance report and display it to the administrator.
When the Order Cancellation function is executed for a selected order, a cancellation event shall be recorded in the Purchase History data entity.
When a customer invokes Add to Cart for selected products, the system shall add the selected product to the Shopping Cart data entity.
The Customer Registration Function shall create and store a new customer account in the Personal Information and Contact Information data entities.
When the system sends an order confirmation email after successful checkout, it shall record the corresponding confirmation event in the Purchase History data entity.
Before the order confirmation email is sent, the Order Confirmation Email Sending Function must have the necessary Order details from the Order data entity.
When a product is added to the shopping cart after availability is confirmed, the system must update the inventory quantity to reflect that addition.
When a new product is added, the system shall store the new product record in the Product Data Entity.
When the Order Cancellation function is executed for a selected order, the order shall be marked as 'Cancelled' in the Order data entity.
Inventory levels shall be updated when the system processes and validates the customer's selected payment method.
The system shall show the customer a confirmation message after the shopping cart creation function completes, following the product availability check confirming that the product can be added.
The system shall adjust inventory levels according to the administrator's order-item action, covering edits, removals, and status updates to items in an order.

After the Product Categorization Function successfully validates the category and updates the association for a product, the product shall be assigned to the selected category in the Category data entity.
When the Checkout Function processes payment, the system shall create an order in the Order data entity.
When a management event is logged, the system shall record that management event in the Purchase History data entity.
When the Checkout Function is executed, the system shall process the payment and store it in the Payment data entity.
The system shall store updated inventory levels in the Inventory data entity when the Inventory Management Function is performed.
The system shall store and associate a successful payment with the order after processing and validating the customer's selected payment method.
The system must validate the submitted email address and check for duplicate customer records before account creation.
The system must validate all submitted registration fields (e.g., name, email, password) before accepting the registration.
If in scope, the system must support viewing or updating Personal Information after registration.
The system must clarify whether a pending registration can be modified or cancelled before account creation.
The system must define whether the confirmation email can be resent on customer request.
The system must define the post-registration operations available to a newly created customer account.
Clarify whether the System is a distinct component requiring an explicit relationship to the Customer Login Function, including its validation and logging responsibilities.
Define the behavior for failed credential validation, including error messaging, retry limits, and whether failed attempts are logged.
Specify the operation that creates or appends a Login Event to Purchase History, including timestamp, customer identifier, and outcome.
Document how login events are written to Purchase History without conflicting with purchase-history operations, including any schema extensions or access rules.
Define the authentication operation that transitions the customer to the Authenticated state, including success criteria and session handling.
Define the customer-initiated login operation, including input validation rules for email and password.
Confirm the authoritative data destination(s) for logout event recording before implementation.
Define the minimum recorded fields for a logout event.
Specify the termination and redirection sequence for logout.
Confirm whether Purchase History is the correct entity for logout event records or whether a dedicated audit log is needed.
Document whether the System performs any logout-related action or remains background context.
Clarify whether logout button UI must satisfy the existing User Interface Specification.
Define the permitted field-level update combinations and whether partial updates are allowed for personal information.
Specify validation rules, error messages, and failure behavior for personal information updates.
Define audit fields such as actor, timestamp, and changed fields for personal information update events.
Specify trigger, recipient, and content requirements for the personal information update confirmation email.
Clarify whether view and update events are distinct and whether viewing personal information must be logged under FR-04.
Document whether 'Validate Changes' is the same validation operation described in FR-04 or a separate validation capability.
Define the system actor's responsibilities across the personal information update workflow.
Clarify whether contact information management includes viewing/retrieving existing contact information, without assuming full CRUD.
Define the validation operation, rules, and error behavior for updated contact information.
Specify the fields and retention requirements for the contact information update event log.
Document the system actor's responsibilities for validation and logging in the contact information update workflow.
Confirm whether 'Validate Changes' is the validation operation used for contact information updates.
Determine if contact information updates are personal information events and whether view events must also be recorded.
The System element should have its retrieval and logging responsibilities for Purchase History Viewing Function explicitly documented.
The Purchase History Viewing Function should specify whether retrieval and display require ordering, pagination, or filtering.
The Viewing Event Recorded event should define the minimum event data to record for purchase-history views.
The Purchase History Displayed state should define empty-state and unavailable-history behavior.
The Customer's purchase-history viewing operation should be constrained to the customer's own records.
The system should document whether product addition triggers the 'Modify Inventory Levels' operation or an inventory initialization operation, including the expected inventory state.
The system should define whether duplicate product names are allowed and, if not, validate against existing products before storing the new product.
The system should ensure that product creation and inventory update either succeed together or provide a defined recovery path.
The system should record the administrator, product identifier, and timestamp for each product addition event.
The system should validate that the selected category exists before associating the new product.
The system should restrict product addition to administrators with the appropriate product management permission.
The system shall update inventory levels when an administrator removes a product.
The system shall validate that no active orders or cart references exist before removing a product.
The system may provide administrators a way to view inventory levels after product removal if post-removal verification is required.
The Remove Product button shall conform to the relevant UI specification when used for product removal.
The system shall enforce any cancellation eligibility constraints when active orders or cart references prevent product removal.
When an administrator changes a product's inventory through FR-09, the system must apply the new inventory level to the product record.
Before persisting updated product information, the system must validate the supplied updated fields against applicable rules if validation is required.
If inventory viewing is part of the update workflow, the system must allow administrators to view current inventory levels before modifying them.
The product information update operation must support updating any of the listed fields as needed.
The system must store updated product information in the Product data entity and record the update event in Purchase History.
Product information update input fields must comply with the applicable user interface specification if UI compliance is in scope.
If product information updates involve personal information changes, the system must record those events appropriately in Purchase History or the relevant event store.
Product information updates may be subject to cancellation eligibility constraints if such constraints apply to the product.
The system performs validation of the selected category before updating the product-category association.
Category assignment or modification changes are validated before the association is updated.
The system validates the selected category as a prerequisite to updating the product-category association.
A category update operation records an audit entry in the Purchase History data entity.
Administrators can assign a category to an uncategorized product and modify an existing category association.
The system should record the association between an administrator's inventory modification and the resulting inventory quantity update and stored inventory level.
The system should provide inventory level viewing from the Inventory data entity for administrators.
The system should validate an administrator's inventory level modification before updating the inventory quantity.
If validation is required, the system should validate inventory level changes before updating the stored inventory quantity.
The system should be documented as the actor that updates inventory quantity and records the management event.
The system should allow administrators to read current inventory levels from the Inventory data entity.
Define the cart-add operation for duplicate products, including whether quantity is incremented or a new line is created.
Specify the system behavior when product availability is not confirmed, such as preventing the add and showing an appropriate message.
Define the inventory update operation semantics for cart additions, including timing and adjustment type.
Clarify the create/update operation applied to the Shopping Cart data entity when adding a product.
Specify confirmation message timing and conditions, including whether it depends on successful cart and inventory updates.
Confirm whether Modify Inventory Levels is in scope for FR-12 and document its relationship if applicable.
Confirm whether the System element should be explicitly associated with FR-12's system actions.
Determine if View Inventory Levels is applicable to the FR-12 inventory workflow and document it only if required.

When a cart modification changes stock, the system must perform the inventory adjustment via the documented Modify Inventory Levels operation, specifying direction and timing for quantity changes and removals.
The system must validate requested quantity changes (e.g., non-negative, within stock limits) before updating the cart and inventory.
The Remove action must define whether the CartItem is deleted or zeroed, and must specify the corresponding inventory adjustment.
The modification event must capture sufficient detail to audit the cart change, including action type, item, old and new quantity, and timestamp.
Define the System's responsibilities for rendering the cart summary and recording the viewing event within the Shopping Cart Viewing Function.
Specify the operation and data fields required to record a cart viewing event in Purchase History.
Define the Read operation needed to retrieve Shopping Cart contents for display, without mandating full CRUD.
The checkout function shall specify the operation that modifies inventory levels after an order is created.
The checkout workflow shall validate changes to cart items, shipping address, and payment method before processing payment.
The checkout function shall record a Personal Information View or Update Event when a customer selects or modifies shipping address or payment method.
The checkout workflow shall specify whether inventory levels are read to validate stock availability before payment and order creation.
The checkout function shall identify the System as the actor responsible for processing payment and creating the order.
The checkout function shall comply with user interface specifications for checkout, address selection, and payment screens.
The System actor must be associated with the Order Confirmation Email Sending Function to perform the automatic email sending.
The system must read order details from the Order data entity to compose the order confirmation email.
The system must create a new EmailRecord entry for each order confirmation email sent.
The system must record the confirmation event in the Purchase History data entity.
The system shall update inventory levels upon successful payment processing.
The system shall process the customer's selected payment method and validate the payment details.
The system shall associate the stored payment record with the corresponding order.
The system shall record the payment event in the Purchase History data entity upon successful payment.
The system shall validate payment details before storing the payment.
The System must validate and activate plugins as part of the Plugin Development Function.
The Plugin Development Function must include a Validate Changes operation to check plugin details before activation.
The system interface update for new plugins must comply with User Interface Specification Compliance.
The system must validate the plugin against defined criteria before activation.
The system must store the plugin in the Plugin data entity upon development or installation.
The system must record the plugin development or installation event in the Purchase History data entity.
If 'Validate Changes' is in scope for plugin configuration, the validation operation should be documented as part of FR-19.
If 'System' is in scope, the responsible system actor for validation and application should be identified.
If UI compliance is in scope, the updated settings interface should satisfy the relevant UI specification.
If validation can fail, the system must reject invalid configuration, leave the Plugin data entity unchanged, and report the validation error.
Configuration events should be recorded in the appropriate audit or history entity; if Purchase History is not intended for configuration events, define separate audit storage.
If audit requirements apply, the configuration event must include administrator identity, timestamp, plugin identifier, and changed settings.
If rollback or audit is required, the previous plugin configuration should be retained or versioned.
If access control is required, only authorized administrators may configure plugin settings and unauthorized attempts should be rejected and audited.
The system shall evaluate each relevant UI element against the defined User Interface Specification and classify it as compliant or non-compliant.
The system shall record each UI compliance check event in the Purchase History data entity, including at least the event timestamp and initiating administrator.
The system shall authorize administrators to initiate UI compliance checks.
The system shall generate and display a compliance report for each completed UI compliance check.
The system shall provide an operation for administrators to initiate a UI compliance check.
The Manage CartItem function should document the applicable operation for validating and applying cart item changes.
If inventory adjustment is in scope, the FR should document the Modify Inventory Levels operation and its trigger from cart changes.
The FR should document whether a Validate Changes operation is required before cart and inventory updates.
The FR should document whether viewing adjusted inventory levels is part of the cart-modification workflow.
If cancellation eligibility applies to cart item removal, the FR should document the constraint and its effect on the update.
If personal information is viewed or updated during cart modification, the FR should document that event.
The system role in cart and inventory updates should be clearly assigned if not already documented.
If UI compliance applies, the FR should reference the applicable UI specification for cart modification controls.
The Manage OrderItem function shall support administrator-initiated edit, remove, and status-update operations as documented.
OrderItem records shall be updated to reflect approved edit, removal, and status-update operations.
Inventory Levels shall be adjusted in response to order item edit, removal, or status-update operations.
A modification event shall be recorded in Purchase History for each order item edit, removal, or status update.
Order item status updates shall follow documented valid transitions and authorization rules.
Only administrators with appropriate permissions shall be allowed to edit, remove, or update order item status.
Purchase History shall record order item modification events and support retrieval for audit or review.
If in scope, the Manage OrderItem function shall trigger a documented inventory adjustment operation; otherwise the trigger shall be documented elsewhere.
The responsible system component for order and inventory updates shall be documented.
The order item management interface shall comply with documented user interface specifications.
Clarify the System actor's responsibility for updating EmailRecord and logging the management event in FR-23.
Verify that Purchase History is the appropriate data entity for email record management audit events; if not, identify or create a dedicated audit/log entity.
Determine whether EmailRecord creation is in scope for FR-23 or covered by a separate function.
Determine whether validation is required for EmailRecord edit or delete operations in FR-23.
FR-24 shall identify the specific system component responsible for displaying email details and logging the viewing event.
The View EmailRecord Function shall provide a read-only view of EmailRecord details; no update or delete operations are implied.
Viewing an email record shall create a Viewing Event record in the Purchase History data entity.
The View EmailRecord Function shall read the selected EmailRecord data entity to display its details.
The View CartItem Function must read the selected cart item's product description, price, and quantity from the CartItem data entity before displaying them.
The View CartItem Function must append a viewing event to the Purchase History data entity whenever cart item details are successfully displayed.
The View CartItem Function must record a viewing event only after the selected cart item details are successfully displayed.
The View CartItem Function must remain read-only and not alter CartItem or Purchase History except for the documented viewing event record.
The System element must be documented as the component responsible for displaying cart item details in the View CartItem Function.
The system shall retrieve payment details from the Payment data entity for display when a payment record is selected, subject to role-based access controls.
The system shall record a payment viewing event in the Purchase History data entity each time payment details are viewed, capturing at least the viewer, timestamp, and payment record identifier.
The View Payment Function shall accept a payment record selection and display payment details, enforcing that customers may view only their own payments and administrators may view all payments.
If payment details include personal information, the system shall record a Personal Information View or Update Event as required by applicable privacy rules.
The payment details display shall comply with the User Interface Specification for formatting, labeling, and presentation.
The System shall be documented as the component responsible for displaying payment details from the Payment data entity upon valid selection.
The system should define business rules for deactivating an administrator account, including account state and access revocation.
The system should record administrator management events in an appropriate audit log with sufficient detail.
Consider documenting the System's role in updating administrator information and recording management events.
Consider documenting whether the Personal Information View or Update Event is raised during administrator account updates.
When an administrator updates a customer's personal information, the system should emit or record a Personal Information View or Update Event.
The system must validate proposed customer account changes before applying them.
The system should check any defined eligibility constraints before deactivating a customer account.
The system must record a management event for each customer account update or deactivation in the Purchase History data entity.
The system must update the applicable customer information data entities based on the fields changed by the administrator.
The system must capture sufficient details in the management event to identify the action and affected customer account.
During category management, the system shall validate the selected category before updating the Category data entity or modifying product associations.
When a category is added, updated, or removed, the system shall modify the associated product associations accordingly.
The system shall record a management event in the Purchase History data entity for each category add, update, or delete action.
The system shall validate category data and update product associations during the Manage Category Function.
If a specific system component is accountable, the FR should document that component for applying and logging UI specification changes.
If compliance is in scope, the FR should document how modified UI specification compliance is verified or recorded.
The system should validate updated UI specification details before applying changes, if validation is required by UI specification management policy.
The system must record each personal information view or update event in the Purchase History data entity with sufficient detail to identify the actor, time, and affected personal information.
The system must validate personal information changes against defined data rules before updating the Personal Information data entity and must handle validation failures appropriately.
The System must validate personal information changes and record the corresponding view or update event in the Purchase History data entity.
The system must allow customers or administrators to view a customer's personal information and must record each view event in the Purchase History data entity.

The system must validate and apply updates to the Personal Information data entity when a customer or administrator updates personal information, and must record the update event in the Purchase History data entity.
The system shall validate proposed contact information changes before updating the Contact Information entity.
The system shall reject invalid contact information changes and shall not update the Contact Information entity.
The system shall support partial updates to Contact Information and preserve fields not included in the update.
The system shall append viewing and update events to Purchase History without modifying or deleting prior history records.
The system shall restrict a customer to viewing and updating only their own contact information.
The system shall allow administrators to view and update contact information for any customer.
The system shall record a distinct event type for contact information view versus contact information update.
The system shall record personal information view or update events in Purchase History when contact information is viewed or updated.
The system shall present a UI-compliant selection and action mechanism for viewing or updating contact information.
The system shall perform validation and event logging for contact information view and update actions.
The cancellation workflow shall enforce and document the eligible status check that gates the Cancel Order action.
The cancellation workflow shall specify the operation that modifies inventory levels and the conditions under which it is invoked.
If order cancellation involves personal information, the workflow shall document the personal information view or update event and its trigger.
The system responsible for updating the order and inventory during cancellation shall be identified and documented.
The order cancellation user interface shall comply with applicable UI specifications for order selection and cancellation actions.
The cancellation workflow shall include validation that the order satisfies the eligible status condition before any change is applied.
The system shall provide a documented way to view inventory levels after cancellation, if required by the workflow.
The Order Cancellation operation shall validate eligible status before updating the order state and inventory levels.
The cancellation workflow shall define the operation that updates inventory levels and results in the Inventory Updated state.
The cancellation workflow shall include an operation that records the cancellation event in Purchase History.
